item.title: Financing the Sustainability Transition: Climate Risk, Capital Allocation, and Financial Innovation
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how financial systems and innovations are addressing the challenges of transitioning to sustainability. The call seeks research on climate risk assessment, the reallocation of capital toward sustainable investments, and the development of financial instruments and mechanisms that support environmental and social objectives.

Appel publié par Finance Research Letters. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Climate risk
  • Capital allocation
  • Financial innovation
  • Sustainability transition
  • Sustainable finance

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Financing Sustainable and Just Transitions: Mechanisms, Accountability and Value Creation
item.content:encoded:
While sustainable finance has expanded as a tool for climate action and capital mobilisation, research has largely focused on aggregate flows rather than how mechanisms are structured and governed. This gap limits understanding of who benefits, how risks are distributed, and whether financial flows reach vulnerable populations or concentrate benefits among well-capitalised actors.

The special issue interrogates institutional practices, governance structures, and implementation processes shaping sustainable finance outcomes. It addresses critical questions about fund allocation decisions, accountability, inclusion of local communities, and adaptability of financial models across diverse contexts, particularly in the Global South.

This collection invites theoretical, empirical, and policy-oriented research reconceptualising sustainable finance as a process of value creation and accountability. The goal is to scrutinise governance frameworks, distributional effects, and capacity to support genuinely fair and inclusive transitions across different contexts.

Appel publié par Corporate Governance. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

item.title: Interdisciplinary Finance in Derivatives Markets
item.content:encoded:
Qingfu Liu, Fudan University

Xinfeng Ruan, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University

This special issue addresses the intersection of interdisciplinary approaches and derivatives markets research. It seeks to move beyond conventional frameworks in asset pricing and risk management by incorporating methods from climate finance, AI, alternative data sources, and machine learning. The focus extends to understanding how derivatives pricing, trading dynamics, and risk allocation contribute to financial stability and market efficiency.

The call welcomes research on climate and green finance applications in derivatives, as well as studies employing emerging technologies such as trustworthy AI, deep learning, and large language models. Beyond these areas, the issue invites broader interdisciplinary perspectives including quantum finance, econophysics, decentralized finance, and biodiversity finance. The special issue is linked to the 15th International Conference on Futures and Other Derivatives, which provides a foundation for attracting high-quality submissions from both academics and practitioners.

Appel publié par Journal of Futures Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Climate risk, extreme weather, and derivatives markets
  • Carbon derivatives and energy transition pricing
  • Multimodal and alternative data in derivatives pricing and forecasting
  • Trustworthy AI and deep learning in derivatives markets
  • Large language models in trading and risk management
  • Quantum finance and physics-inspired pricing models
  • Econophysics and complex systems in market dynamics
  • Decentralized finance and financial innovation
  • Price discovery and volatility dynamics
  • Risk transmission and hedging efficiency
  • Corporate finance and asset pricing

Timeline

  • February 28, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Forecasting for a Sustainable Future: Energy Systems, Climate Risks, Environmental Governance, Financial Markets and Societal Resilience
item.content:encoded:
Goutte Stephane, Université Paris Saclay

This special issue addresses the fragmentation between environmental sciences, energy systems, public health, and finance by promoting integrated forecasting methodologies capable of anticipating cascading systemic risks. Research communities need to develop common predictive frameworks that capture complex feedback mechanisms linking environmental governance, ecosystem services, financial markets and societal resilience under unprecedented uncertainty.

The special issue welcomes innovations in econometric, statistical, machine learning and artificial intelligence approaches using novel data sources such as satellite imagery and alternative data. Key focus areas include electricity system resilience under renewable integration, carbon market forecasting, natural capital accounting, sustainable finance, and the distributional impacts of energy transitions.

Contributions are sought globally with emphasis on emerging and developing economies perspectives. The collection will comprise 10-12 peer-reviewed articles demonstrating methodological diversity and practical relevance for policymakers, regulators, investors and sustainability managers.

Appel publié par Journal of Forecasting. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
